messages:
maya: Heads-up — around 11:12 UTC we saw a QPS spike in eu-west that left ~120 pods Pending for ~2m. HPA target metric (external/custom-qps) dropped to 0 briefly and HPA did not scale. CA also didn't add nodes because the node pool hit preemptible capacity limits.

jordan: @maya do we have metric export logs? any missing samples from the custom-metric adapter?

sam: checking now. Preliminary — looks like prometheus-exporter to stackdriver dropped some samples for ~45s (network retransmits). ExternalMetricValue shows no data => HPA interpreted as 0.

olga: ouch. So HPA scaled-down logic kicked in then? or HPA just stayed at current replicas?

sam: HPA saw a sudden low metric and did not scale up (it scales on > target). Meanwhile CA wanted to add nodes but nodepool is preemptible and we exhausted surge capacity. CA logs say "scale-up blocked: node quota exhausted".

ryan: autoscale-bot reports: \"CA attempt: add 4 gpu-nodes -> failed (quota)\". We fell back to heavier CPU-only path for some requests but tail latency spiked ~1.2s.

jordan: can we temporary-mitigate by enabling metric-stabilization or use an alternative metric (cpu/requests) as fallback in HPA? Also maybe increase nodepool surge or use non-preemptible pool for critical services.

maya: Agreed. Short term: 1) add stabilizationWindowSeconds to HPA to ignore brief drops, 2) add a second metric in HPA (cpu) as fallback, 3) increase preemptible pool max surge to allow CA to add nodes while we triage.

olga: example HPA snippet I propose:```yaml
apiVersion: autoscaling/v2
kind: HorizontalPodAutoscaler
metadata:
  name: model-server-hpa
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    apiVersion: apps/v1
    kind: Deployment
    name: model-server
  minReplicas: 4
  maxReplicas: 50
  metrics:
  - type: External
    external:
      metric:
        name: custom-qps
      target:
        type: AverageValue
        averageValue: "100"
  - type: Resource
    resource:
      name: cpu
      target:
        type: Utilization
        averageUtilization: 70
  behavior:
    scaleUp:
      stabilizationWindowSeconds: 60
      policies:
      - type: Percent
        value: 200
        periodSeconds: 60
```

sam: Also recommend exporter retry/backoff tuning. The gap came from the exporter hitting transient network errors and backoff was too aggressive.

jordan: For CA side: temporarily increase nodepool "maxSurge" and add a small non-preemptible fallback pool with a very small min nodes (1-2) and taint+preferNoSchedule so only critical deployments use it.

maya: Cost note — non-preemptible fallback will add ~$1.6k/mo per node (gpus) in eu-west. We should only enable for critical customer-facing model-serving.

autoscale-bot: CA alert created: incident/3223 - "scale-up blocked: quota". Policy assigned to @sam and @ryan.

ryan: I'll open a quota request with cloud tomorrow AM and flip maxSurge for the preemptible pool to +4 now. Also will add the fallback nodepool manifest to infra repo in a branch for review.

olga: For medium-term: run a small chaos test to simulate metric drop and ensure HPA+CA stability, and add local smoothing in exporter (emit last-known if short gap) so HPA doesn't see a hard 0.

maya: Action items: @sam — tweak exporter retry/backoff and add last-known-fallback; @ryan — surge + fallback pool + quota request; @olga — PR for HPA behavior changes; I'll notify product teams of possible small SLA blip.

jordan: thanks. tagging this as learnings for runbook: add a section 'external metric outages -> fallback metrics + CA surge policies'. :memo:

sam: update — exporter patch ready, will roll tomorrow in canary.

maya: cool. closing thread once surge & HPA patch live. :thumbsup:
